name: CA-43
label: Safe D

key_factors: Long-serving incumbent Maxine Waters running for reelection
Republican challenger Cristian Morales with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Waters at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: The +27 Democratic district lean, Waters' incumbency, and her clear fundraising advantage over an opponent with no reported receipts all point to an overwhelming Democratic win, and prediction markets agree at about 96%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected surge in challenger fundraising would be the only plausible route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maxine Waters, a longtime Democratic incumbent, is seeking reelection in a Los Angeles-area district with a +27 Democratic partisan lean. She advanced to the general election against Republican Cristian Morales, who reports no fundraising, while Waters has raised about $864,000 and holds a large cash advantage. No outside groups are spending against her.

There are no public general-election polls or expert ratings for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets price Waters at roughly 96 percent to win. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the only uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
